recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core FHIR source change is needed for FHIR-13193; future extension discoverability changes should be handled in the Extension Pack or IG Publisher/resource-page linking design while respecting the later FHIR-16525/FHIR-20637 link-based direction.
issue_request: FHIR-13193 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core change request following GForge tracker #10460. It said the prior visibility work did not make extensions whose contexts apply to all resources or elements discoverable from resource extension views, using resource-pertainsToGoal and MedicationRequest as the motivating example.
initial_application: The Jira comment records SVN revision 12703. In git this is 01e6e8a758a8914622fcab563fbe03b4d4dbd236, '#10460 - generic extensions cross-linked', which added publisher logic for generic all-resource/all-element extension rows and reference-any extension rows on resource extension pages.
additional_context: FHIR-12667 is the concrete MedicationRequest/Goal question that exposed the discoverability problem and confirmed resource-pertainsToGoal was the intended extension. The extension now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack with context element/Resource, while current core resource pages link to Extension Pack extension lists. Later FHIR-13656, FHIR-16525, and FHIR-20637 visibility decisions favor resource-page links over inline extension tables.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current core template still has the generated extension-link hook, the Extension Pack generates per-resource extension pages, and the current MedicationRequest extension page lists resource-pertainsToGoal with Resource context.

related_jiras.note: MedicationRequest/Goal question that demonstrated resource-pertainsToGoal was hard to discover and led to the FHIR-13193 follow-up.
Later STU3 extension-visibility issue already audited on the combined branch and confirming resource-page extension links as the intended visibility mechanism.
Reconsidered listing standard extensions inline on each content page and rejected that as too prominent/noisy, preferring links.
Accepted the later option to highlight extensions below resource content views, reinforcing the link-based design.
